title.zh: 卷一百七十五 列傳第一百 竇劉二張楊熊柏
title.en: Volume 175 Biographies 100: Dou, Liu, two Zhangs, Yang, Xiong, Bai
title.raw: 卷一百七十五 列傳第一百 竇劉二張楊熊柏 Volume 175 Biographies 100: Dou, Liu, two Zhangs, Yang, Xiong, Bai

sentences.zh: 竇劉二張楊熊柏

translations.literal: Dou, Liu, the two Zhangs, Yang, Xiong, and Bai
translations.idiomatic: Dou, Liu, the two Zhangs, Yang, Xiong, and Bai

sentences.zh: 竇群，字丹列，京兆金城人。

translations.literal: Dou Qun, styled Danlie, was a native of Jincheng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Qun, whose style name was Danlie, came from Jincheng in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父叔向，以詩自名，代宗時，位左拾遺。

translations.literal: His father Shuxiang made a name for himself through poetry; in Emperor Daizong's reign he held the post of Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuxiang was famed for his verse; under Emperor Daizong he served as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 群兄弟皆擢進士第，獨群以處士客隱毗陵。

translations.literal: Qun's brothers all passed the jinshi examination, but Qun alone, as a reclusive gentleman, lodged in seclusion at Piling.
translations.idiomatic: All of Qun's brothers won the jinshi degree; he alone lived as a retired scholar in hiding at Piling.

sentences.zh: 母卒，嚙一指置棺中，廬墓次，終喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he bit off one finger and placed it in the coffin, kept vigil beside the tomb, and observed the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death he severed a finger and laid it in her coffin, dwelt in a mourning hut by the grave, and completed the full mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 從盧庇傳啖助《春秋》學，著書數十篇。

translations.literal: He studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Lu Pi, who transmitted the teachings of Tan Zhu, and wrote several dozen treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Lu Pi in the Tan Zhu school of Spring and Autumn studies and composed several dozen works.

sentences.zh: 蘇州刺史韋夏卿薦之朝，並表其書，報聞，不召。

translations.literal: Suzhou prefect Wei Xiaqing recommended him to court and jointly memorialized his writings; the court acknowledged receipt but did not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wei Xiaqing of Suzhou recommended him to the throne and submitted his books together with the recommendation; the court took note but did not call him in.

sentences.zh: 後夏卿入為京兆尹，復言之德宗，擢為左拾遺。

translations.literal: Later, when Xiaqing entered the capital as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he spoke of him again to Emperor Dezong, who promoted him to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaqing later became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he spoke for him again to Dezong, who appointed him Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時張薦持節使吐蕃，乃遷群侍御史，為薦判官，入見帝曰：「陛下即位二十年，始自草茅擢臣為拾遺，何其難也？

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jian was commissioner to Tibet; Qun was transferred to Attending Censor and made Jian's aide. On entering audience he said to the emperor: "Your Majesty, in the twenty years since you took the throne you have only now raised me from common obscurity to Reminder—how hard that was!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jian held credentials as envoy to Tibet, Qun was moved to Attending Censor and made his judicial aide. He appeared before the emperor and said, "Sire, in twenty years on the throne you have only now lifted me from the thatched hut to Reminder—how rare such advancement is!

sentences.zh: 以二十年難進之臣為和蕃判官，一何易？

translations.literal: Yet to make a man so hard to advance over twenty years the judicial aide for pacifying Tibet—how easy that is!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would make a man you found so hard to promote over twenty years the aide for a Tibetan peace mission—how lightly you treat such a post!

sentences.zh: 」帝壯其言，不遣。

translations.literal: " The emperor was impressed by his words and did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was stirred by his remonstrance and did not dispatch him.

sentences.zh: 王叔文黨盛，雅不喜群，群亦忄幸忄幸不肯附。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen's faction was powerful and naturally disliked Qun; Qun too was resentful and unwilling to attach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen's party was ascendant and had little regard for Qun; Qun in turn sullenly refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 欲逐之，韋執誼不可，乃止。

translations.literal: They wished to drive him out, but Wei Zhiyi would not agree, and the matter stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to expel him, but Wei Zhiyi objected, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 群往見叔文曰：「事有不可知者。

translations.literal: Qun went to see Shuwen and said, "There are matters one cannot foresee.
translations.idiomatic: Qun went to Shuwen and said, "Some things cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 」叔文曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: " Shuwen said, "What then?
translations.idiomatic: " Shuwen asked, "What do you mean?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「去年李實伐恩恃權，震赫中外，君此時逡巡路傍，江南一吏耳。

translations.literal: " He said, "Last year Li Shi relied on favor and wielded power, shaking court and realm; you then lingered by the roadside—a mere clerk of south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Last year Li Shi abused grace and monopolized authority, terrifying the empire; you were then hesitating on the roadside—no more than a petty official south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 今君又處實之勢，豈不思路傍復有如君者乎？

translations.literal: Now you stand in Shi's position—will you not consider that by the roadside there may again be someone like you?
translations.idiomatic: Now you occupy Shi's place—have you not thought that someone like you may again be waiting by the roadside?

sentences.zh: 」叔文悚然，亦卒不用。

translations.literal: " Shuwen was startled, and in the end did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuwen was shaken, and in the end never used him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，轉膳部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, Qun was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites and concurrently Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong he became Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous business.

sentences.zh: 出為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 節度使於頔聞其名，與語，奇之，表以自副。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Yu Di heard his reputation, spoke with him, found him extraordinary, and memorialized to have him as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioner Yu Di, hearing of him, conversed with him, marveled at him, and requested him as personal aide.

sentences.zh: 武元衡、李吉甫皆所厚善，故召拜吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanheng and Li Jifu were both well disposed toward him, so he was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng and Li Jifu both favored him, and he was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元衡輔政，薦群代為中丞。

translations.literal: When Yuanheng served as chief minister, he recommended Qun to succeed him as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng, as chief minister, recommended Qun to replace him as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 群引呂溫、羊士諤為御史，吉甫以二人躁險，持不下。

translations.literal: Qun brought in Lü Wen and Yang Shie as censors; Jifu regarded the two as rash and dangerous and withheld approval.
translations.idiomatic: Qun nominated Lü Wen and Yang Shie as censors; Jifu judged them reckless and would not confirm them.

sentences.zh: 群忮狠，反怨吉甫。

translations.literal: Qun was jealous and fierce, and turned to resent Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was spiteful and turned his resentment on Jifu.

sentences.zh: 吉甫節度淮南，群謂失恩，因擠之。

translations.literal: When Jifu was made military commissioner of Huainan, Qun believed he had lost favor and pressed against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu went out to Huainan as military commissioner, Qun thought he had fallen from grace and worked to squeeze him out.

sentences.zh: 陳登者，善術，夜過吉甫家，群即捕登掠考，上言吉甫陰事。

translations.literal: Chen Deng, skilled in occult arts, passed Jifu's house by night; Qun at once arrested Deng and tortured him for confession, memorializing that Jifu had secret dealings.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Chen Deng, versed in divination, visited Jifu's house at night; Qun seized him, tortured him, and accused Jifu of clandestine affairs.

sentences.zh: 憲宗面覆登，得其情，大怒，將誅群，吉甫為救解，乃免，出為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Xianzong confronted Deng in person, learned the truth, was greatly enraged, and was about to execute Qun; Jifu pleaded for him and he was spared, being sent out as Huainan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong examined Deng face to face, learned the facts, flew into a rage and nearly put Qun to death; Jifu interceded, he was spared, and was demoted to observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 改黔中。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His post was changed to Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 會水壞城郛，調溪洞群蠻築作，因是群蠻亂，貶開州刺史。

translations.literal: When floods destroyed the walls, he levied the tribal peoples of the streams and caves for construction labor; on that account the tribes rebelled, and he was demoted to prefect of Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Floods ruined the ramparts; he drafted the stream-dwelling tribes for repair work, the tribes rose in disorder, and he was demoted to prefect of Kai.

sentences.zh: 稍遷容管經略使。

translations.literal: He was gradually moved to military commissioner of Rongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to military commissioner of Rongguan.

sentences.zh: 召還，卒於行，年五十五，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he died on the journey at age fifty-five; he was posthumously given the title of Left Regular Cavalryman-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned back, he died on the road at fifty-five and was posthumously made Left Regular Cavalryman-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 群狠自用，果於復怨。

translations.literal: Qun was fierce and self-willed, and ruthless in repaying grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was harsh, willful, and swift to settle scores.

sentences.zh: 始召，將大任之，眾皆懼，及聞其死，乃安。

translations.literal: When he was first summoned, the court was about to entrust him with great office and all were afraid; when word came of his death, people were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: At first his recall promised high appointment and everyone feared him; when he died, the court breathed easier.

sentences.zh: 兄常、牟，弟庠、鞏，皆為郎，工詞章，為《聯珠集》行於時，義取昆弟若五星然。

translations.literal: His elder brothers Chang and Mou and younger brothers Ku and Gong all served as court gentlemen, excelled in belles-lettres, and compiled the Linked Pearls, which circulated in their day—the title likening the brothers to five stars.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brothers Chang and Mou and younger brothers Ku and Gong all held gentleman posts, were skilled writers, and issued the Linked Pearls, comparing the brothers to five stars.

sentences.zh: 常，字中行，大歷中及進士第，不肯調，客廣陵，多所論著，隱居二十年。

translations.literal: Chang, styled Zhongxing, passed the jinshi in the Dali era, refused appointment, lodged at Guangling, wrote extensively, and lived in seclusion twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, style name Zhongxing, took the jinshi under Dali, declined office, stayed at Guangling writing, and remained in retirement twenty years.

sentences.zh: 鎮州王武俊聞其才，奏辟不應。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou, hearing of his talent, memorialized to recruit him, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou, hearing of his gifts, invited him to his staff, but Chang would not come.

sentences.zh: 杜佑鎮淮南，署為參謀。

translations.literal: When Du You governed Huainan, he appointed him staff planner.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, as Huainan commissioner, made him a staff planner.

sentences.zh: 歷朗夔江撫四州刺史、國子祭酒，致仕。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Lang, Kui, Jiang, and Fu and as Director of the Directorate of Education, then retired.
translations.idiomatic: He held prefectures of Lang, Kui, Jiang, and Fu, became Director of the Directorate of Education, and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈越州都督。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Governor-General of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was posthumously made Governor-General of Yue.

sentences.zh: 牟，字貽周，累佐節度府。

translations.literal: Mou, styled Yizhou, repeatedly served on military commissioners' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Mou, style name Yizhou, served many times on frontier staffs.

sentences.zh: 晚從昭義盧從史，從史浸驕，牟度不可諫，即移疾歸東都。

translations.literal: Late in life he followed Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi; as Congshi grew arrogant, Mou judged that he could not be admonished and pleaded illness to return to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he followed Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi; when Congshi grew insolent, Mou saw counsel would fail, feigned illness, and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 從史敗，不以覺微避去自賢。

translations.literal: When Congshi was defeated, he did not claim credit for having sensed trouble and withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Congshi fell, Mou did not parade his early withdrawal as wisdom.

sentences.zh: 位國子司業。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 庠，字胄卿，終婺州刺史。

translations.literal: Ku, styled Zhouqing, ended as prefect of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ku, style name Zhouqing, died as prefect of Wu.

sentences.zh: 鞏，字友封，雅裕，有名於時。

translations.literal: Gong, styled Youfeng, was refined and generous and famed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, style name Youfeng, was cultivated and openhanded and enjoyed renown.

sentences.zh: 平居與人言若不出口，世號「囁嚅翁」。

translations.literal: In ordinary conversation with others he seemed scarcely to speak; the age called him the Muttering Old Man.
translations.idiomatic: In daily talk he seemed barely to open his mouth; contemporaries dubbed him the Muttering Old Man.

sentences.zh: 元稹節度武昌，奏鞏自副，卒。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zhen was military commissioner at Wuchang, he memorialized for Gong as his deputy; Gong died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen, commissioner at Wuchang, had Gong appointed his aide; Gong died in that post.

sentences.zh: 劉棲楚，其出寒鄙。

translations.literal: Liu Qichu came from humble and mean origins.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu sprang from poor and low birth.

sentences.zh: 為鎮州小吏，王承宗奇之，薦於李逢吉，繇鄧州司倉參軍擢右拾遺。

translations.literal: He was a petty clerk in Zhenzhou; Wang Chengzong admired him and recommended him to Li Fengji, by whom he was raised from Dengzhou warehouse aide to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: A minor clerk in Zhenzhou, he won Wang Chengzong's notice, was recommended to Li Fengji, and rose from Dengzhou warehouse aide to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 逢吉之罷裴度、逐李紳，皆嗾而為奸者。

translations.literal: Fengji's dismissal of Pei Du and expulsion of Li Shen were both urged on by Qichu as his crafty accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji's ouster of Pei Du and banishment of Li Shen were both driven by Qichu as his scheming henchman.

sentences.zh: 敬宗立，視朝常晏，數遊畋失德。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he was tardy at morning audience and often went hunting in neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingzong, audiences were habitually late and the emperor often hunted to the neglect of rule.

sentences.zh: 棲楚諫曰：「惟前世王者初嗣位，皆親庶政，坐以待旦。

translations.literal: Qichu remonstrated: "Former sage-kings at the beginning of their reigns all personally attended to common affairs, sitting to await the dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu admonished: "Ancient kings at the start of their reigns personally handled government, sitting up to await dawn.

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位，安臥寢內，日晏乃作。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly taken the throne yet lies at ease within the inner apartments, not rising until the sun is high.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty, newly enthroned, rests in the inner quarters and does not rise until late morning.

sentences.zh: 大行殯宮密邇，鼓吹之聲日聞諸朝。

translations.literal: The late emperor's coffin hall is close by, and the sound of funeral music daily reaches the court.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's mourning hall is near, and dirges daily resound through the palace.

sentences.zh: 且憲宗及先帝皆長君，朝夕恪勤，四方猶有叛者。

translations.literal: Moreover, both Emperor Xianzong and the prior emperor were mature rulers who toiled diligently morning and evening, yet rebellion still arose in the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong and the previous emperor were seasoned rulers who labored dawn to dusk, yet rebels still rose on every side.

sentences.zh: 陛下以少主，踐祚未幾，惡德流布，恐福祚之不長也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is a young sovereign who has barely ascended; ill repute spreads abroad—I fear your fortune will not long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a young ruler newly enthroned; bad conduct is already rumored—I fear your blessing will not last.

sentences.zh: 臣以諫為官，使陛下負天下譏，請碎首以謝。

translations.literal: I hold the office of remonstrator; if Your Majesty bears the world's reproach, I beg to dash my head and atone.
translations.idiomatic: As remonstrator, if Your Majesty earns the empire's censure, I ask to dash out my brains in atonement.

sentences.zh: 」遂額叩龍墀，血被面。

translations.literal: " He then struck his forehead on the imperial steps until blood covered his face.
translations.idiomatic: " He then beat his brow on the dragon pavement until his face ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉傳詔：「毋叩頭，待詔旨。

translations.literal: Li Fengji transmitted the edict: "Do not knock your head; await the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji relayed the decree: "Cease knocking your head; await the throne's word.

sentences.zh: 」棲楚捧首立，帝動容，揚袂使去。

translations.literal: " Qichu held his head and stood; the emperor was moved, waved his sleeve, and had him withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: " Qichu stood clutching his head; the emperor was stirred, gestured dismissal, and had him led away.

sentences.zh: 棲楚曰：「不聽臣言，臣請死於此。

translations.literal: Qichu said, "If Your Majesty will not heed my words, I ask to die here.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu said, "If you will not hear me, I beg to die on this spot.

sentences.zh: 」有詔尉諭，乃出。

translations.literal: " An edict comforted him, and he then left.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict soothed him, and only then did he withdraw.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎，辭疾歸洛。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Diarist, then resigned on grounds of illness and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Diarist, pleaded illness, and retired to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後諫官對延英，帝問：「向廷爭者在邪？

translations.literal: Later, when remonstrators faced the emperor in the Yanying Hall, the emperor asked, "Is the man who disputed in court present?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when remonstrators met the emperor at Yanying, he asked, "Is the one who quarreled in court here?

sentences.zh: 」以諫議大夫召。

translations.literal: " He was summoned as Remonstrator of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: " He was recalled as Remonstrator of the Left.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宣授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was directly appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received direct appointment as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 故事，侍郎無宣授者，逢吉喜助己，故不次任之。

translations.literal: By precedent vice ministers were not directly appointed; Fengji was pleased that he aided him, and so gave him this extraordinary post.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent vice ministers were not directly commissioned; Fengji, glad of his support, broke precedent to elevate him.

sentences.zh: 數月，改京兆尹，峻誅罰，不避權豪。

translations.literal: After several months he was made metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, severe in punishment and unafraid of the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, harsh in penalties and fearless of magnates.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸惡少竄名北軍，淩藉衣冠，有罪則逃軍中，無敢捕。

translations.literal: Before this, vicious youths had enrolled in the northern armies, bullying the gentry; when guilty they fled into the army and none dared arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: Hoodlums had hidden in the northern armies, insulting the gentry; on crime they fled to the camps and none dared seize them.

sentences.zh: 棲楚一切窮治，不閱旬，宿奸老蠹為斂跡。

translations.literal: Qichu prosecuted them all to the end; within ten days the entrenched villains shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu pursued every case to the limit; within ten days old evils drew in their claws.

sentences.zh: 一日，軍士乘醉有所淩突，諸少年從旁噪曰：「癡男子，不記頭上尹邪？」

translations.literal: One day a soldier, drunk, committed some outrage; the youths nearby shouted, "Fool—don't you remember the magistrate on your head?"
translations.idiomatic: Once a drunken soldier caused a disturbance; youths nearby yelled, "Idiot—have you forgotten the magistrate above your head?"

sentences.zh: 然其性詭激，敢為怪行，乘險抵巇，若無顧藉，內實恃權怙寵以幹進。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was devious and impulsive; he dared strange acts, courting peril on sheer cliffs as if he had nothing to lose, while inwardly he relied on power and favor to force advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was perverse and rash, performing shocking stunts and courting danger as if fearless, while inwardly he leaned on patronage to claw upward.

sentences.zh: 詣宰相，厲色慢辭，韋處厚惡之，出為桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: Visiting the chief ministers, he spoke with fierce looks and insolent words; Wei Chuhou detested him and sent him out as Guiguan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the chancellors' offices he glared and spoke rudely; Wei Chuhou loathed him and posted him to Guiguan as observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Left Regular Cavalryman-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given Left Regular Cavalryman-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 張又新，字孔昭，工部侍郎薦之子。

translations.literal: Zhang Youxin, styled Kongzhao, was son of Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Youxin, style name Kongzhao, was the son of Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jian.

sentences.zh: 元和中，及進士高第，歷左右補闕。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he took high honors in the jinshi examination and served as Left and Right Supplementation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe he placed high on the jinshi and served as Left and Right Supplementation Officer.

sentences.zh: 性傾邪。

translations.literal: His nature was crooked.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature devious.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉用事，惡李紳，冀得其罪，求中朝兇果敢言者厚之，以危中紳。

translations.literal: Li Fengji held power, hated Li Shen, and hoped to find crime in him; he sought fierce and bold men at court who dared speak and richly rewarded them to endanger Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji, hating Li Shen, sought grounds against him, found bold speakers at court, and richly paid them to imperil Shen.

sentences.zh: 又新與拾遺李續、劉棲楚等為逢吉搏吠所憎，故有「八關十六子」之目。

translations.literal: Youxin, with Reminder Li Xu and Liu Qichu, were hated by Fengji's pack for their attacks, hence the label "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."
translations.idiomatic: Youxin, with Li Xu and Liu Qichu, were detested as Fengji's attack dogs, earning the name "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."

sentences.zh: 敬宗立，紳貶端州司馬，朝臣過宰相賀，閽者曰：「止，宰相方與補闕語，姑伺之。

translations.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, Shen was demoted to Sima of Duanzhou; as courtiers passed the chancellor to congratulate, the doorkeeper said, "Stop—the chancellor is speaking with the Supplementation Officer; wait a moment.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzong's accession Shen was demoted to Duanzhou Sima; officials coming to congratulate the chancellor were told, "Wait—the chancellor is with the Supplementation Officer.

sentences.zh: 」及又新出，流汗揖百官曰：「端溪之事，竊不敢讓。

translations.literal: " When Youxin came out, sweating, he bowed to the officials and said, "As for the affair at Duanxi, I dare not disclaim credit.
translations.idiomatic: " When Youxin emerged, drenched in sweat, he bowed to the officials: "The Duanxi affair—I dare not deny my part.

sentences.zh: 」人皆辟易畏之。

translations.literal: " All shrank back in fear of him.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone recoiled in dread.

sentences.zh: 尋轉祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘗買婢遷約，為牙儈搜索陵突，御史劾舉，逢吉庇之，事不窮治。

translations.literal: Once, buying a slave girl, he broke the contract; the broker searched and insulted him; the censorate impeached him, but Fengji shielded him and the case was not fully pursued.
translations.idiomatic: He once bought a maidservant then reneged; the broker searched and humiliated him; censors impeached him, but Fengji protected him and the matter was not pressed.

sentences.zh: 及逢吉罷，領山南東道節度，表又新為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Fengji fell from power and took the Huainan east circuit command, he had Youxin as his campaign staff Sima.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengji lost office and went to Huainan east circuit, he took Youxin as campaign Sima.

sentences.zh: 坐田伾事，貶汀州刺史。

translations.literal: For involvement in Tian You's affair he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in Tian You's case, he was demoted to prefect of Ting.

sentences.zh: 李訓有寵，又新復見用，遷刑部郎中，為申州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Xun gained favor, Youxin was again employed, made Director in the Ministry of Justice, and sent as prefect of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xun rose, Youxin was restored, made Director of Justice, and sent to Shen as prefect.

sentences.zh: 訓死，復坐貶。

translations.literal: When Xun died, he was again demoted for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun's death he was demoted again.

sentences.zh: 終左司郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as Left Department Director.
translations.idiomatic: He finished as Left Department Director.

sentences.zh: 又新善文辭，再以諂附敗，喪其家聲雲。

translations.literal: Youxin was skilled in letters but twice ruined his family name through flattery and attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Youxin wrote well yet twice destroyed his house's reputation by fawning on power.

sentences.zh: 楊虞卿，字師臯，虢州弘農人。

translations.literal: Yang Yuqing, styled Shigao, was a native of Hongnong in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuqing, style name Shigao, came from Hongnong in Guo.

sentences.zh: 父寧，有高操，談辯可喜。

translations.literal: His father Ning possessed lofty integrity and was pleasant in debate and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning was high-minded, eloquent, and engaging in discourse.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，調臨渙主簿，棄官還夏，與陽城為莫逆交。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination, was appointed chief clerk of Linhuai, resigned, returned to Xia, and became sworn friend with Yang Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ning passed the Mingjing, served as Linhuai chief clerk, quit office, returned home to Xia, and became Yang Cheng's closest friend.

sentences.zh: 德宗以諫議大夫召城，城未拜，詔寧即諭，與俱來。

translations.literal: Dezong summoned Cheng as Remonstrator of the Left; Cheng had not yet accepted; the emperor ordered Ning at once to persuade him, and they came together.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong summoned Cheng as Left Remonstrator; before Cheng accepted, the throne ordered Ning to urge him, and both arrived.

sentences.zh: 陜虢觀察使李齊運表置幕府。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of Shan-Guo, memorialized to place him on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioner Li Qiyun of Shan-Guo placed him on staff.

sentences.zh: 齊運入為京兆尹，表奉先主簿，拜監察御史，坐累免。

translations.literal: When Qiyun became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he recommended him as chief clerk of Fengxian; he was made Attending Censor and dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiyun became Jingzhao magistrate, he recommended Ning as Fengxian chief clerk; Ning became Attending Censor but was dismissed for a fault.

sentences.zh: 順宗初，召為殿中侍御史，終國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzong's reign he was summoned as Attending Censor within the Palace and died as Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzong's reign he was recalled as Palace Attending Censor and died as Director of Education.

sentences.zh: 虞卿第進士、博學宏辭，為校書郎。

translations.literal: Yuqing passed the jinshi and the erudite macrocosmic examination and served as collator.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing took jinshi and erudite macrocosmic degrees and served as collator.

sentences.zh: 抵淮南，委婚幣焉，會陳商葬其先，貧不振，虞卿未嘗與遊，悉所賫助之。

translations.literal: Going to Huainan, he entrusted betrothal gifts; Chen Shang was burying his forebears and was too poor to manage it—Yuqing had never associated with him yet gave all he carried to help.
translations.idiomatic: Bound for Huainan with betrothal gifts, he found Chen Shang burying his ancestors too poor to proceed; though strangers, Yuqing gave all he had to aid him.

sentences.zh: 擢累監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初立，逸遊荒恣，虞卿上疏曰：「烏鳶遭害仁鳥逝，誹謗不誅良臣進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong first took the throne, indulging in roaming pleasures and reckless abandon, Yuqing memorialized: "When crows and kites suffer harm the benevolent birds depart; when slander is not punished worthy ministers advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Muzong's accession, given to idle roaming and dissipation, Yuqing submitted: "When carrion birds are harmed, the virtuous birds flee; when calumny goes unpunished, good ministers come forward.

sentences.zh: 臣敢冒誅獻瞽言。

translations.literal: Your servant dares risk execution to offer blind counsel.
translations.idiomatic: I dare risk death to offer my humble counsel.

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯、舜以天下為憂，不以位為樂。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Yao and Shun took the empire's cares as their own and did not treat the throne as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Yao and Shun worried for the realm rather than rejoiced in their rank.

sentences.zh: 況今北虜方梗，西戎弗靖，兩河有瘡痏之虞，五嶺罹氛厲之役。

translations.literal: Moreover, the northern barbarians are now obstructive, the western tribes unsettled, the two He regions face the peril of running sores, and the Five Ridges suffer pestilence and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The northern enemy blocks the frontier, the western tribes are unquiet, the two He circuits bear festering troubles, and the Five Ridges labor under plague and levy.

sentences.zh: 人之疾苦積下，朝之制度莫脩。

translations.literal: The people's suffering accumulates below, while the court's institutions are not repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Popular hardship piles up below, yet court institutions go unmended.

sentences.zh: 邊亡見儲，國用浸屈，固未可以高枕而息也。

translations.literal: The borders show empty stores, state revenue daily contracts—truly one cannot rest high on a pillow and be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Border granaries stand empty and the treasury shrinks; one cannot pillow one's head high and sleep in peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下初臨萬幾，宜有憂天下心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly assumed the myriad affairs; you ought to have a heart that worries for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just taken the myriad reins; you should bear the empire in mind.

sentences.zh: 當日見輔臣公卿百執事，垂意以問，使四方內外灼有所聞。

translations.literal: Each day you should receive chief ministers, dukes, and the hundred officials, showing concern in inquiry, so that within and without all clearly hear.
translations.idiomatic: Meet your chief ministers, nobles, and the hundred officers daily, question them with care, and let the realm see it plainly.

sentences.zh: 而聽政六十日，入對延英，獨三數大臣承聖問而已，它內朝臣偕入齊出，無所咨詢。

translations.literal: Yet in sixty days of hearing government, entering audience at Yanying, only three or four great ministers received the sacred inquiry; other inner-court officials entered and left together with no consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in sixty days at court, at Yanying audiences only a few senior ministers heard your questions; the rest of the inner officials filed in and out with no counsel sought.

sentences.zh: 諫臣盈廷，忠言不聞，臣實羞之。

translations.literal: Remonstrators fill the hall yet loyal words are not heard—I am truly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrators crowd the hall yet loyal speech never reaches you—I am ashamed of it.

sentences.zh: 蓋主恩疏而正路塞也。

translations.literal: This is because imperial favor is distant and the upright path blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial grace has grown remote and the straight road is blocked.

sentences.zh: 公卿大臣宜朝夕燕見，則君臣情接而治道得矣。

translations.literal: Dukes and great ministers ought to be received morning and evening in easy audience, so that ruler and minister join in feeling and the way of rule is attained.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers should meet you morning and evening in relaxed audience, so feeling joins between ruler and servant and governance is secured.

sentences.zh: 今宰臣四五人，或頃刻侍坐，鞠躬隕越，隨旨上下，無能往來，此繇君太尊、臣太卑故也。

translations.literal: Now four or five chief ministers sometimes sit for a moment, bowing with bodies bent low, rising and falling at the imperial will, unable to exchange words—this is because the lord is too exalted and the servants too low.
translations.idiomatic: Today four or five chancellors may sit a moment, bowing until they nearly fall, bobbing at your nod, unable to speak freely—because the throne is too lofty and the servants too abject.

sentences.zh: 公卿列位，雖陟降清地，曾未奉優眷、承下問。

translations.literal: The ranks of dukes, though promoted to pure posts, have never received gracious favor or answered inquiry from below.
translations.idiomatic: The ranked nobles, though raised to exalted posts, have never tasted your gracious notice or your questioning ear.

sentences.zh: 雖陛下神聖如五帝，猶宜周爰顧逮，惠以氣色，使支體相成，君臣昭明。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty is as sagely as the Five Emperors, you should still look about with care, show a kindly countenance, and make limbs and trunk work together so ruler and minister are bright to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you are as sage as the Five Emperors, you should still look widely, show a warm face, and knit trunk and limbs so ruler and minister shine upon each other.

sentences.zh: 陛下求治於宰相，宰相求治於臣等，進忠若趨利，論政若訴冤，此而不治，無有也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty seeks good rule from the chancellor; the chancellor seeks good rule from us; if advancing loyalty is like rushing profit and discussing government like pleading wrongs, with this there will be no failure to govern.
translations.idiomatic: You seek order from the chancellor, the chancellor from us; if loyalty is pursued like profit and policy debated like a grievance, nothing will remain ungoverned.

sentences.zh: 自古天子居危思安之心同，而居安慮危之心則異，故不得皆為聖明也。

translations.literal: From antiquity the hearts of sons of Heaven in peril thinking of safety are the same, but in safety thinking of peril they differ—hence not all can be sage and bright.
translations.idiomatic: In danger all rulers think of safety alike, but in safety their thoughts of peril differ—so not every throne is sage.

sentences.zh: 」時又有衡山布衣趙知微，亦上書指言帝倡優在側，馳騁無度，內作色荒，外作禽荒。

translations.literal: " At the time the commoner Zhao Zhiwei of Hengshan also memorialized, pointing out that the emperor kept actors at his side, rode and hunted without limit, made inner lewdness and outer bird-chasing excess.
translations.idiomatic: " Meanwhile Zhao Zhiwei, a Hengshan commoner, also wrote, accusing the emperor of keeping entertainers at hand, hunting without restraint, indulging lust within and sport without.

sentences.zh: 辭頗危切，帝詔宰相尉謝。

translations.literal: His words were very sharp; the emperor ordered the chancellor to comfort and thank him.
translations.idiomatic: His language was severe; the emperor had the chancellor console and thank him.

sentences.zh: 宰相因是賀天子納諫，然不能用也。

translations.literal: The chancellor therefore congratulated Heaven's Son on accepting remonstrance, yet the advice could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor then congratulated the throne on heeding criticism, but nothing was acted upon.

sentences.zh: 俄詔行勞西北邊。

translations.literal: Soon an edict sent him to comfort the northwest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to tour and comfort the northwest border.

sentences.zh: 還，遷侍御史，改禮部員外郎、史館脩撰。

translations.literal: On return he was made Attending Censor, then Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he became Attending Censor, then Vice Director of Rites and Historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 進吏部。

translations.literal: He advanced to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會曹史李賨等鬻偽告，調官六十五員，贓千六百萬以上，虞卿發其奸，賨等系御史府。

translations.literal: When clerks Li Bin and others sold false appointment notices, adjusting sixty-five offices, with bribes above sixteen million, Yuqing exposed the fraud and Bin and the rest were held in the censorate prison.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks led by Li Bin sold forged appointment notices for sixty-five posts, taking more than sixteen million in bribes; Yuqing exposed them and they were jailed in the censorate.

sentences.zh: 而虞卿親吏嘗受二百萬，亡命，私奴受三十萬，虞卿縛奴送獄。

translations.literal: Yet Yuqing's personal clerk had once taken two million and fled; a private slave took three hundred thousand—Yuqing bound the slave and sent him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: His own clerk had taken two million and fled; a household slave took three hundred thousand—Yuqing tied the slave and sent him to jail.

sentences.zh: 三司嚴休復、高鉞、韋景休雜推，賨等皆誅死。

translations.literal: The Three Offices—Yan Xiufu, Gao Qian, and Wei Jingxiu—jointly tried the case; Bin and the rest were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices, Yan Xiufu, Gao Qian, and Wei Jingxiu, jointly judged them; Bin and his fellows were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 虞卿坐不檢下免官。

translations.literal: Yuqing was dismissed for not restraining subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing lost office for failing to discipline his staff.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，引為右司郎中、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru held government, they brought him in as Right Department Director and Erudite of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru he became Right Department Director and Hongwen academician.

sentences.zh: 再遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 虞卿佞柔，善諧麗權幸，倚為奸利。

translations.literal: Yuqing was fawning and supple, skilled at pleasing the powerful with witty grace, relying on them for illicit gain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing was pliant and flattering, adept at charming favorites, and traded on them for corrupt profit.

sentences.zh: 歲舉選者，皆走門下，署第註員，無不得所欲，升沈在牙頰間。

translations.literal: Each year those seeking selection all ran to his gate; he annotated ranks and posts, and none failed to get what they wished—promotion and demotion lay on the tip of his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Annual candidates thronged his door; he marked ranks and posts, and none missed his favor—advancement or ruin hung on his word.

sentences.zh: 當時有蘇景胤、張元夫，而虞卿兄弟汝士、漢公為人所奔向，故語曰：「欲趨舉場，問蘇、張；

translations.literal: At the time there were Su Jingyin and Zhang Yuanfu, but Yuqing's brothers Rushi and Hangong were where men rushed, hence the saying: "If you wish to hurry to the examination ground, ask Su and Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: Su Jingyin and Zhang Yuanfu still mattered, but Yuqing's brothers Rushi and Hangong drew the crowds, so people said: "For the examination field, ask Su and Zhang;

sentences.zh: 蘇、張猶可，三楊殺我。

translations.literal: Su and Zhang are still tolerable—the three Yangs will kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Zhang may suffice—the three Yangs will ruin you.

sentences.zh: 」宗閔待之尤厚，就黨中為最能唱和者，以口語軒輊事機，故時號「黨魁」。

translations.literal: " Zongmin treated him especially well; among the faction he was the best at echoing and harmonizing, weighing affairs by gossip, hence the nickname "Faction Chief."
translations.idiomatic: " Zongmin favored him most; in the clique he led the chorus and steered affairs by rumor, earning the title "Faction Chief."

sentences.zh: 德裕之相，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: When Deyu became chancellor, Yuqing was sent out as prefect of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu took the chancellorship, Yuqing was posted to Changzhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 宗閔復入，以工部侍郎召，遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Zongmin returned to power, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Works and made metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin's return brought him back as Vice Minister of Works and Jingzhao magistrate.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，京師訛言鄭註為帝治丹，剔小兒肝心用之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe, the capital rumor said Zheng Zhu was making elixir for the emperor, gouging out small boys' livers and hearts for use.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year nine the capital rumored that Zheng Zhu brewed elixir for the emperor by cutting out children's livers and hearts.

sentences.zh: 民相驚，扃護兒曹。

translations.literal: The people were alarmed and barred their children indoors.
translations.idiomatic: Families panicked and locked their children in.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，註亦內不安，而雅與虞卿有怨，即約李訓奏言：「語出虞卿家，因京兆騶伍布都下。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; Zhu was uneasy within, and having long hated Yuqing, joined Li Xun in memorializing that the talk came from Yuqing's house, spread by the Jingzhao courier runners through the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered; Zhu, ill at ease and hostile to Yuqing, with Li Xun claimed the tale began in Yuqing's household and was spread by Jingzhao runners.

sentences.zh: 」御史大夫李固言素嫉虞卿周比，因傅左端倪。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Li Guyin had long detested Yuqing's cliquishness and seized on slight signs.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Guyin, who loathed Yuqing's faction ties, seized on loose ends.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下虞卿詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and sent Yuqing to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and imprisoned Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 於是諸子弟自囚闕下稱冤，虞卿得釋，貶虔州司戶參軍，死。

translations.literal: Then the sons and brothers imprisoned themselves below the palace gate crying injustice; Yuqing was released, demoted to Qianzhou army aide, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and brothers then chained themselves at the palace gate pleading injustice; he was freed, demoted to Qianzhou army aide, and died.

sentences.zh: 子知退、知權、壇、堪、漢公，皆擢進士第，漢公最顯。

translations.literal: Sons Zhituo, Zhiquan, Tan, Kan, and Hangong all passed the jinshi; Hangong was most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Zhituo, Zhiquan, Tan, Kan, and Hangong all took the jinshi; Hangong shone brightest.

sentences.zh: 漢公，字用乂。

translations.literal: Hangong, styled Yongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Hangong, style name Yongyi.

sentences.zh: 始辟興元李絳幕府，絳死，不與其禍。

translations.literal: He first entered the staff of Li Jiang of Xingyuan; when Jiang died, he did not share in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He began on Li Jiang's Xingyuan staff; when Jiang perished, he escaped the purge.

sentences.zh: 遷累戶部郎中、史館修撰，轉司封郎中。

translations.literal: He rose through Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Historiography compiler to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced from Revenue Director and Historiography compiler to Rites Director.

sentences.zh: 坐虞卿，下除舒州刺史，徙湖、亳、蘇三州。

translations.literal: For Yuqing's guilt he was demoted to prefect of Shu, then moved through Hu, Bo, and Su.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated through Yuqing, he was demoted to Shu prefect, then served Hu, Bo, and Su.

sentences.zh: 擢桂管、浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: He was raised to observation commissioner of Guiguan and Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He became observation commissioner of Guiguan and Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 繇戶部侍郎拜荊南節度使，召為工部尚書。

translations.literal: From Vice Minister of Revenue he was made military commissioner of Jingnan and summoned as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: From Revenue Vice Minister he was made Jingnan military commissioner, then recalled as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 或劾漢公治荊南有貪贓，降秘書監。

translations.literal: Some impeached him for corruption governing Jingnan, and he was reduced to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of graft in Jingnan, he was demoted to Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 稍遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was gradually moved to Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Director of Education.

sentences.zh: 宣宗擢為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong promoted him to prefect of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong appointed him prefect of Tong.

sentences.zh: 於是，給事中鄭裔綽、鄭公輿共奏漢公冒猥無廉概，不可處近輔，三還制書。

translations.literal: Then Supervising Censors Zheng Yichuo and Zheng Gongyu jointly memorialized that Hangong was shameless and without integrity, unfit for close service, and three times returned the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censors Zheng Yichuo and Zheng Gongyu then wrote that Hangong was brazen and corrupt, unfit for the inner court, and thrice returned the appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 帝它日凡門下論執駁正未嘗卻。

translations.literal: On other days whenever the Secretariat debated and rejected, the emperor never overruled.
translations.idiomatic: On ordinary days the throne never overruled Secretariat objections.

sentences.zh: 漢公素結左右，有奧助。

translations.literal: Hangong had long cultivated the inner attendants and had hidden backers.
translations.idiomatic: Hangong had long cultivated palace eunuchs who backed him in secret.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝惑不從，制卒行。

translations.literal: This time the emperor was swayed and did not heed them; the edict was finally issued.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor wavered and ignored them; the appointment stood.

sentences.zh: 會寒食宴近臣，帝自擊球為樂，巡勞從臣，見裔綽等曰：「省中議無不從，唯漢公事為有黨。

translations.literal: At a Cold Food feast for close ministers the emperor himself played ball for sport, touring to comfort his followers, and seeing Yichuo and the rest said: "The Secretariat has never refused my word except on Hangong's affair—there is faction at work.
translations.idiomatic: At a Cold Food feast he played ball himself, greeted his intimates, and told Yichuo and the others: "You never oppose me except over Hangong—that is faction.

sentences.zh: 」裔綽獨對：「同州，太宗興王地。

translations.literal: Yichuo alone replied: "Tongzhou is the land where Taizong rose as king.
translations.idiomatic: Yichuo alone answered: "Tong was where Taizong began his kingship.

sentences.zh: 陛下為人子孫當精擇守長付之，漢公既以墨敗，陛下容可舉劇部私貪人？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, as descendant, ought to choose governors with care; Hangong has already failed for corruption—can Your Majesty appoint a greedy man to a great post for private reasons?
translations.idiomatic: As his descendant you should choose governors carefully; Hangong is already stained by ink—can you give a major post to a known grafter for favor?

sentences.zh: 」帝恚見顏間。

translations.literal: " The emperor's anger showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: " Anger flickered on the emperor's face.

sentences.zh: 翌日，斥裔綽為商州刺史。

translations.literal: The next day Yichuo was demoted to prefect of Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Yichuo was sent out as Shang prefect.

sentences.zh: 漢公自同州更宣武、天平兩節度使，卒。

translations.literal: Hangong moved from Tong to the two commands of Xuanwu and Tianping and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hangong went from Tong to Xuanwu and Tianping as military commissioner and died.

sentences.zh: 子籌、範，仕亦顯。

translations.literal: Sons Chou and Fan also rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Chou and Fan likewise achieved distinction.

sentences.zh: 汝士，字慕巢。

translations.literal: Rushi, styled Muchao.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi, style name Muchao.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，又擢宏辭。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and also won the erudite macrocosmic examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi and also the erudite macrocosmic degree.

sentences.zh: 牛李待之善，引為中書舍人。

translations.literal: The Niu and Li factions treated him well and made him Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The Niu-Li factions favored him and made him Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 開成初，繇兵部侍郎為東川節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he went from Vice Minister of War to military commissioner of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaicheng he rose from War Vice Minister to Dongchuan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時嗣復鎮西川，乃族昆弟，對擁旄節，世榮其門。

translations.literal: At the time Sifu governed Xichuan—they were clan brothers, each holding a command, and the age gloried their house.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu then held Xichuan; as kinsmen they faced each other with banners, and the world honored their clan.

sentences.zh: 終刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He ended as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 子知溫、知至，悉以進士第入官。

translations.literal: Sons Zhiwen and Zhizhi all entered office through the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Zhiwen and Zhizhi entered service by jinshi.

sentences.zh: 知溫終荊南節度使。

translations.literal: Zhiwen ended as military commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen finished as Jingnan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 知至為宰相劉瞻所善，以比部郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: Zhizhi was favored by Chancellor Liu Zhan, made Drafting Drafter from Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi, cherished by Liu Zhan, became Drafting Drafter from Revenue Director.

sentences.zh: 瞻得罪，亦貶瓊州司馬，擢累戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhan fell, Zhizhi was also demoted to Sima of Qiongzhou, then gradually rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan was ruined, Zhizhi was demoted to Qiongzhou Sima, then climbed again to Revenue Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 楊氏自汝士後，貴赫為冠族。

translations.literal: After Rushi the Yang clan became the most illustrious of great houses.
translations.idiomatic: From Rushi onward the Yangs became the foremost noble house.

sentences.zh: 所居靜恭裏，兄弟並列門戟。

translations.literal: At their residence in Jinggong Lane the brothers each displayed gate halberds.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinggong Lane the brothers each bore gate halberds.

sentences.zh: 咸通後，在臺省方鎮率十餘人。

translations.literal: After Xiantong more than ten of them held posts in the central bureaus or as frontier commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiantong more than ten held capital or frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 張宿者，本寒人，自名諸生。

translations.literal: Zhang Su came from humble origins yet styled himself a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su was born poor yet called himself a literatus.

sentences.zh: 憲宗為廣陵王時，因張茂宗薦尉，得出入邸中，誕譎敢言。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was Prince of Guangling, through Zhang Maozong's recommendation as aide he gained access to the prince's residence, crafty and bold in speech.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Guangling, Xianzong took him in through Zhang Maozong as aide; he entered the mansion, sly and outspoken.

sentences.zh: 及監撫，自布衣授左拾遺，交通權幸，四方賂遺滿門。

translations.literal: When appointed heir he was raised from common cloth to Left Reminder, trafficked with the powerful, and bribes from the four quarters filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: On becoming heir apparent he rose from commoner to Left Reminder, courted favorites, and gifts from every quarter clogged his door.

sentences.zh: 數召對，不能慎密，坐漏禁中語，貶郴丞十餘年。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience many times, he could not keep secrets and was demoted to Chen prefecture aide for more than ten years for leaking palace speech.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience repeatedly, he could not hold his tongue and was demoted to Chen aide for over ten years for leaking inner-court words.

sentences.zh: 累遷比部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Revenue Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉數言其狡譎不可信，白為濠州刺史，宿上疏自言，留不遣。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Fengji often said he was cunning and untrustworthy and had him made prefect of Hao; Su memorialized on his own behalf and was kept from going.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji often called him treacherous and had him sent to Hao as prefect; Su petitioned in his own defense and was kept at court.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以為諫議大夫，逢吉曰：「諫議職要重，當待賢者。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make him Remonstrator of the Left; Fengji said: "The remonstrator's post is weighty and should await a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted him as Left Remonstrator; Fengji said: "That office is weighty and should go to a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 宿細人，不可使汙是官。

translations.literal: Su is a petty man—he must not be allowed to stain that office.
translations.idiomatic: Su is a small man and must not defile it.

sentences.zh: 陛下必用之，請先去臣乃可。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must use him, please remove me first.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on using him, remove me first.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 後逢吉罷，詔權知諫議大夫，宰相崔群、王涯同請曰：「諫議大夫，前世或自山林、擢行伍任之者，然皆道義卓異於時。

translations.literal: Later when Fengji fell, an edict made Su acting Remonstrator of the Left; chancellors Cui Qun and Wang Ya jointly petitioned: "The remonstrator of old was sometimes taken from mountain forests or promoted from the ranks, yet all were outstanding in conduct for their age.
translations.idiomatic: After Fengji's fall an edict made Su acting Left Remonstrator; Cui Qun and Wang Ya petitioned together: "Remonstrators of old came from reclusion or the army, yet all stood out in conduct.

sentences.zh: 今宿望輕，若待以不次，未足以寵，適以累之也。

translations.literal: Now Su's reputation is slight; if you favor him with an extraordinary appointment, it is not enough to honor him—it only harms him.
translations.idiomatic: Su's standing is light; an exceptional appointment will not honor him—only harm him.

sentences.zh: 」請授他官，不聽，使中人宣授焉。

translations.literal: " They asked another office be given; the emperor would not listen and had a eunuch announce the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " They asked another post; the emperor refused and a eunuch proclaimed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 宿怨執政不與己，乃日肆讒甚，與皇甫镈相附離，多中傷正人君子。

translations.literal: Su resented the rulers for not siding with him and daily poured out slander, attaching himself to Huangfu Bo and striking at upright gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Su hated the chancellors for not backing him and daily slandered, clinging to Huangfu Bo and wounding upright men.

sentences.zh: 元和末，持節至淄青，李師道願割地遣子入侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe he held credentials to Ziqing; Li Shidao wished to cede territory and send his son to court as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanhe he bore credentials to Ziqing; Li Shidao offered to yield land and send his son to court.

sentences.zh: 既而悔，復遣宿往，暴卒於道，贈秘書監。

translations.literal: Then he repented and sent Su again; Su died violently on the road and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He then regretted it and sent Su again; Su died suddenly on the road and was posthumously made Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 熊望者，字原師，擢進士第。

translations.literal: Xiong Wang, styled Yuanshi, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wang, style name Yuanshi, took the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 性險躁，以辯說遊公卿間。

translations.literal: His nature was dangerous and impetuous; he traveled among dukes and ministers by eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: He was rash and treacherous, moving among grandees by debate.

sentences.zh: 劉棲楚為京兆尹，樹權勢，望日出入門下，為刺取事機，陰佐計畫。

translations.literal: When Liu Qichu was metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao he built power; Wang daily entered his gate, spying out affairs and secretly aiding his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: As Qichu built power as Jingzhao magistrate, Wang came and went daily, picking up intelligence and plotting in secret.

sentences.zh: 敬宗喜為歌詩，議置東頭學士，以備燕狎。

translations.literal: Jingzong delighted in composing songs and poems and discussed establishing Eastern Head Academicians for intimate revelry.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong loved verse and talked of Eastern Head academicians for private amusement.

sentences.zh: 棲楚薦望，未及用，帝崩。

translations.literal: Qichu recommended Wang, but before appointment the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu recommended Wang, but before the post was filled the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，韋處厚秉政，詔望因緣險薄，營密職，圖褻幸，讙沸眾議，貶漳州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne Wei Chuhou held government and edicted that Wang, by treacherous shallowness, sought secret office and imperial favor, stirring public clamor, be demoted to Qiongzhou army aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wenzong, Wei Chuhou ruled and condemned Wang for scheming toward secret posts and imperial intimacy; the uproar sent him to Qiongzhou as army aide.

sentences.zh: 柏耆者，有縱橫學。

translations.literal: Bai Ji possessed the arts of alliance and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ji mastered alliance and stratagem.

sentences.zh: 父良器，為時威名將。

translations.literal: His father Liangqi was a famed general of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangqi was a renowned general of the time.

sentences.zh: 耆誌健而望高，急於立名。

translations.literal: Ji was ambitious in spirit and high in reputation, eager to make a name.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was vigorous and ambitious, hungry for renown.

sentences.zh: 是時，王承宗以常山叛，朝廷厭兵，耆杖策詣淮西行營謁裴度，且言願得天子一節馳入鎮，可掉舌下之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Chengzong rebelled at Changshan; the court was weary of war. Ji took staff in hand, went to Pei Du's Huainan west circuit camp, and said he wished to obtain one imperial credential to gallop into the garrison and could bring it down with a wag of the tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong had rebelled at Changshan while the court wearied of war; Ji visited Pei Du's western Huainan headquarters and vowed that with a single imperial commission he could talk the garrison into submission.

sentences.zh: 度為言，乃以左拾遺往。

translations.literal: Du spoke for him, and he was sent as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Du endorsed him, and he went out as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 既至，以大誼動承宗，至泣下。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he moved Chengzong with great righteousness until Chengzong wept.
translations.idiomatic: He moved Chengzong with lofty argument until the rebel wept.

sentences.zh: 乃請獻二州，以二子入質。

translations.literal: Chengzong then offered to surrender two prefectures and send two sons as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong then offered two prefectures and sent two sons as hostages.

sentences.zh: 真擢耆左拾遺，由是聲震一時。

translations.literal: The emperor promoted Ji to Left Reminder, and from this his fame shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: The throne made him Left Reminder, and his name thundered across the realm.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Diarist.

sentences.zh: 王承元徙義成軍，遣諫議大夫鄭覃往慰成德軍，賚緡錢百萬。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengyuan was moved to the Yicheng army, Remonstrator of the Left Zheng Tan was sent to comfort the Chengde army, bearing a million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengyuan was shifted to Yicheng; Remonstrator Zheng Tan was sent to comfort Chengde with a million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 賚未至，舉軍嘩議，穆宗遣耆諭天子意，眾乃信悅。

translations.literal: Before the gift arrived the whole army clamored; Muzong sent Ji to explain the Son of Heaven's intent, and the host then trusted and rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The bounty had not arrived when the army erupted; Muzong sent Ji to proclaim the emperor's intent, and the troops were reassured.

sentences.zh: 轉兵部郎中、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was made Director in the Ministry of War and Remonstrator of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to War Director and Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 太和初，李同捷反，詔兩河諸鎮出兵，久無功。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Li Tongjie rebelled; an edict ordered the two He circuits to raise troops, but for long there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe, Li Tongjie rebelled; troops from the two He circuits were ordered out, yet victory lingered.

sentences.zh: 乃授耆德州行營諸軍計會使，與判官沈亞之諭旨。

translations.literal: Ji was then made Commissary for the Dezhou campaign armies of the two He circuits, and with judicial aide Shen Yazhi conveyed the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was appointed commissary of the Dezhou field armies and, with aide Shen Yazhi, delivered the throne's orders.

sentences.zh: 會橫海節度使李祐平德州，同捷窮，請降，祐使大將萬洪代守滄州，同捷未出也，耆以三百騎馳入滄，以事誅洪，與同捷朝京師。

translations.literal: When Transverse Sea military commissioner Li You pacified Dezhou, Tongjie was cornered and sought surrender; You had great general Wan Hong hold Cangzhou in his stead while Tongjie had not yet departed. Ji galloped into Cang with three hundred horsemen, executed Hong on the facts of the case, and escorted Tongjie to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li You of Transverse Sea took Dezhou; Tongjie, desperate, offered to yield. You left Wan Hong to hold Cangzhou while Tongjie lingered; Ji raced in with three hundred riders, killed Hong, and brought Tongjie to court.

sentences.zh: 既行，諜言王廷湊欲以奇兵劫同捷，耆遂斬其首以獻。

translations.literal: After they set out, spies said Wang Tingcou meant to seize Tongjie with surprise troops; Ji then cut off his head and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: As they marched, word came that Wang Tingcou would ambush Tongjie; Ji beheaded Tongjie and presented the head.

sentences.zh: 諸將嫉耆功，比奏攢詆，文宗不獲已，貶耆循州司戶參軍、亞之南康尉。

translations.literal: The generals envied Ji's merit and jointly memorialized slander; Wenzong, unable to refuse, demoted Ji to Xunzhou army aide and Yazhi to Nan Kang aide.
translations.idiomatic: Generals jealous of Ji's glory piled accusations; Wenzong, constrained, demoted Ji to Xunzhou army aide and Yazhi to Nan Kang aide.

sentences.zh: 宦人馬國亮譖耆受同捷先所得王稷女及奴婢珍貲。

translations.literal: Eunuch Ma Guoliang slandered Ji for taking Tongjie's prior prize—the daughter of Wang Ji—and slave girls with precious goods.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Ma Guoliang accused Ji of taking Tongjie's spoils—Wang Ji's daughter and treasured slaves.

sentences.zh: 初，祐聞耆殺洪，大驚，疾遂劇。

translations.literal: Earlier, when You heard Ji had killed Hong, he was greatly shocked and his illness grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: When You first heard Ji had killed Hong, he was stunned and his illness worsened.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「祐若死，是耆殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If You dies, it is Ji who killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If You dies, Ji has killed him.

sentences.zh: 」至是，積前怒，詔長流愛州，賜死。

translations.literal: " By then, with prior anger accumulated, an edict exiled him far to Aizhou and ordered death by gift.
translations.idiomatic: " Now, anger piled upon anger, an edict banished him to Aizhou and commanded him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：詩人斥譖人最甚，投之豺虎、有北，不置也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The poets rebuke slanderers most harshly—cast them to wolves and tigers, send them to the northern waste, do not spare them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: The Odes condemn slanderers most fiercely—throw them to wolves and tigers, drive them to the northern wilds, show no mercy.

sentences.zh: 如群、棲楚輩則然，肆訐以示公，構黨以植私，其言纚纚若可聽，卒而入於敗亂也。

translations.literal: Men like Qun and Qichu are just so: they freely accuse to show public virtue and build factions to plant private gain; their words flow smoothly as if worth hearing, yet in the end they enter ruin and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Qun and Qichu do the same—parade accusation as public duty, knit factions for private ends; their speech glides like truth, yet ends in ruin.

sentences.zh: 孔子所謂「順非而澤」者歟，「利口覆邦家」者歟？

translations.literal: Are they not those Confucius called "smooth-tongued in wrong" and "sharp-mouthed overturners of state and clan"?
translations.idiomatic: Are they not Confucius's "pliant in wrong yet glossy of tongue" and "clever mouths that overturn kingdom and house"?

sentences.zh: 耆掩眾取功，自速其死，哀哉！

translations.literal: Ji concealed the host to seize merit and hastened his own death—pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Ji stole the army's credit and rushed to his doom—how lamentable!
